title: Cajun Potato Soup with Bacon & Smoked Sausage
creator: Mississippi Kween (mississippi_kween / Mississippikweenofficial)
cookTime: Not fully specified (bacon about 5 minutes on sear/saute, then simmer until potatoes are very soft; simmer time not stated)
ingredients: 1 lb bacon, cut up (regular or thick cut)
1 lb smoked sausage, cut into rounds
Garlic, minced ("a ton"; amount not stated)
About 5 lb yellow potatoes, diced, skins on (she used 3 lb in the video)
2 cups shredded cheddar cheese, plus extra for topping
instructions: Step 1: Set a multi-cooker (or large pot) to sear/saute. Cook the cut-up bacon until very crispy (about 5 minutes in, she adds the sausage).
Step 2: Add the smoked sausage and cook until the bacon and sausage are crispy, then drain the grease.
Step 3: Add the onion and cook until soft, then add the garlic.
Step 4: Pour in 4 cups chicken broth and 4 cups water.
Step 5: Add the potatoes, switch to simmer, and season with Cajun seasoning, salt, and pepper so the potatoes absorb it. Cover and cook until the potatoes are very soft.
Step 6: Stir in 2 cups heavy whipping cream and 2 cups shredded cheddar. Turn the heat to its lowest setting and keep stirring until the cheese is fully melted.
Step 7: Mash a good portion of the potatoes right in the pot with a big fork to thicken the soup, leaving plenty of chunks.
Step 8: Serve topped with a little more cheddar.
notes: From a Mississippi Kween Facebook reel captioned 'The best #potatosouprecipe is right here and you need to make it for #soupseason'. The caption has no written recipe and Facebook comments were behind a login wall, so the recipe comes from the creator's narration and description in what is very likely the same video on her YouTube channel (https://www.youtube.com/shorts/WB-4OJ13STQ, 'Creamy Potato Soup - SOUP SEASON Is HERE!', posted Oct 20, 2026, same ~2:24 length); the match is likely but not 100% confirmed. She cooks it in an 8-quart multi-cooker and says the recipe is in her cookbook 'Krockpots to Kasseroles'. Unclear: garlic and seasoning amounts, the exact Cajun seasoning brand, simmer time, and servings aren't stated.
